channel.title: Giao Nguyen
channel.description: Giao Nguyen is a .NET software engineer with 10+ years of experience building web, cloud and machine-integrated systems.

item.title: 7 Levels of .NET Mastery
item.description: A map of seven skill levels for .NET developers, from C# fundamentals to running reliable production systems, with what to learn at each step and how to tell you are ready for the next.

item.title: Habits that keep C# code readable
item.description: Five small habits that make C# code easier to read, review and change six months later.

item.title: How to Diagnose a Memory Leak in .NET
item.description: A step-by-step method to confirm a memory leak, capture evidence with dotnet-counters and dotnet-gcdump, and trace the objects back to the root that keeps them alive.

item.title: How to Find the Cause of a Production Performance Issue
item.description: A repeatable method for turning "the site is slow" into a specific cause, by narrowing down the layer first and using traces, counters and database tools second.

item.title: How to Handle Concurrent Requests Safely
item.description: Why two requests at the same time can corrupt your data, and how to prevent it at each layer: in memory, in the database and across multiple servers.

item.title: How to Recover from Downstream Service Failure
item.description: How to keep your service healthy when a service it depends on is slow or down, using timeouts, retries, circuit breakers, fallbacks and queues.

item.title: Level 1: C# Fundamentals
item.description: The base of everything in .NET. What to learn in C#, the habits that keep code correct from day one, and a practice plan to prove you are ready for Level 2.

item.title: Level 2: Types and OOP Design
item.description: How to model a problem with clear types. Classes, structs and records, interfaces, composition over inheritance, and the SOLID principles used as guidelines.

item.title: Level 3: Collections and LINQ
item.description: Choosing the right collection by cost, writing LINQ that is correct and readable, and understanding deferred execution, the source of many subtle bugs.

item.title: Level 4: Async and Concurrency
item.description: What async and await really do, how to avoid blocking and deadlocks, how to cancel and limit work, and how to share state between threads safely.

item.title: Level 5: ASP.NET Core and Data Access
item.description: Building a web API that behaves under load. The request pipeline, dependency injection lifetimes, validation, authentication, and writing EF Core code you can trust.

item.title: Level 6: Performance and Runtime Internals
item.description: How the .NET runtime works, how to measure instead of guess, and how to reduce allocations and CPU cost where it matters, using BenchmarkDotNet and diagnostic tools.

item.title: Level 7: Production Systems and Reliability
item.description: Everything that happens after the code compiles. Observability, resilience, safe deployments, configuration, data changes on live systems, and handling incidents.

item.title: A checklist for debugging production issues
item.description: A calm, repeatable order of questions to work through when something breaks in production.
